(for all $k,m,n\in E$, with the fraction understood to be $0$ when $k+m+n=0$).

**Derivation.** Write $k=2a$, $m=2b$, $n=2c$, $S=a+b+c$, and $f(a,b,c)=T(2a,2b,2c)$. Then $f=2S$ when $abc=0$, while for $a,b,c\ge1$,
$$f=3+\tfrac16\sum_{\text{6 neighbours}}f,$$
where neighbours are obtained by shifting one unit between coordinates (preserving $S$). Since any function of $S$ alone has zero discrete Laplacian $\Delta g=\frac16\sum g_{\rm nbr}-g$, set $f=2S+u$. Then $u|_{abc=0}=0$ and $\Delta u=-3$. By symmetry try $u=C\,abc$. A direct computation gives $\frac16\sum a'b'c'=abc-\frac S3$, so $\Delta(abc)=-S/3$; hence $-CS/3=-3$, i.e. $C=9/S$. Thus $f=2S+\frac{9abc}{S}$, which returns to the boxed formula. The boundary case $kmn=0$ is satisfied automatically, and uniqueness on each level set $k+m+n$ follows from the maximum principle for the discrete Dirichlet problem.
